source_law.title: Stopping, standing or parking prohibited in specified places (1)(i)
source_law.text: A person shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with law or the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device, in any of the following places: Within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad.

runtime_uncertainties: Six park/stop/stand cases have exact primary and justified fallback offline constructions, but no original Native rail capture or decoded public compatibility fixture.
Eight traffic-conflict, other-law, police-direction and official-device cases remain unconstructed.
Nearest physical rail identity, actual stop/stand/park action, traffic necessity and authority require original source review.
Semantic proposals, recorded-only processing and independent audits remain pending.

drv.standing_or_parked.evidence: Per-frame measured speed and rest timeline, with vehicle state requiring later Native verification.

st.railway_crossing.evidence: Both surveyed physical rail polylines with stable rail IDs; map/native survey remains to be acquired.

rel.centre_distance.evidence: Replaced center proxy with minimum body footprint-to-nearest-rail distance; 15.24 m is the statutory 50-foot comparison, not an invented threshold.

rel.occupies.evidence: Resting footprint and frame map establish where the body occupied space at each measured instant.

kin.extent.evidence: Four vehicle footprint corners sourced from pose and bounding box; no center-point proxy.

drv.forced_halt.evidence: Traffic-conflict reason remains a separate sourced Native control/actor trace; the meter retains unknown reasons rather than inferring an exception.

legal_analysis_note: Fourteen branch cases are planned across seven comparisons; only six park/stop/stand cases have scoped offline proofs. No original physical rail or legal outcome is asserted.
physical_prerequisites: Measure vehicle stopping/standing/parking footprint to the nearest physical railroad rail across the 50-foot boundary.
legal_interpretation_limit: The nearest rail, not the crossing center or an abstract sign, defines distance.
